preservedEvidenceNotes: The awake-versus-sleep split is the defining disclosure of this preserved edge: the only adjusted association is AWAKE bruxism (OR 3.38, CI 1.01-11.27 in a 38-versus-38 sample) and the same model reports a SLEEP BRUXISM NULL, so the umbrella target's sleep member is prevalence-context only. Landing this edge would give bruxism-awake-sleep (a zero-suggestion draft mapping) its first registered incoming edge. nexusClaim.associationBasis: Authoring registers this relationship only as the bounded association the located orofacial literature supports, with the awake-versus-sleep split stated first: a 2024 case-control study (38 PTSD patients and 38 controls, PTSD by SCID-I/P, bruxism by Research Diagnostic Criteria Axis II) reports AWAKE bruxism associated with PTSD at adjusted OR 3.38 (95 percent CI 1.01-11.27, p = 0.047) while SLEEP BRUXISM WAS NOT ASSOCIATED with any covariate in the same model, and PTSD predicted current orofacial pain (IRR 3.01, 95 percent CI 1.38-6.55) (PMID 38363350); a 2022 cross-sectional assessment of 673 patients attending a specialized PTSD clinic before treatment reports painful TMD in 28.4 percent, awake bruxism in 48.3 percent and sleep bruxism in 40.1 percent against general-population figures of 8.0, 31.0 and 15.3 percent (all p < 0.001), with PTSD symptom severity only POORLY correlated with each (rs 0.126, 0.155 and 0.084) and with trauma-type gradients (sexual assault with awake bruxism, physical violence with sleep bruxism) (PMID 36056716); and a 2020 retrospective pilot of 71 Israeli combat PTSD veterans (mean age 60.7 years) reports parafunctional activity signs in 90 percent, periodontal disease in 100 percent (66 percent severe) and a significant parafunction-by-severe-periodontal association (P = 0.035) (PMID 32577706). The registered claim is the narrowest these anchors jointly permit: that PTSD is associated with elevated prevalence of awake bruxism and parafunctional oral activity, with the awake-bruxism signal the only adjusted association in the located evidence and the sleep-bruxism component resting on prevalence and trauma-type gradients alone.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of bruxism is established for any individual: the only adjusted association in the located evidence is for AWAKE bruxism and its confidence interval is wide and near the null (OR 3.38, 95 percent CI 1.01-11.27, p = 0.047 in a 38-versus-38 convenience sample), and the same model found SLEEP BRUXISM not associated with any covariate; the prevalence anchor correlates PTSD symptom severity only poorly with bruxism severity (rs at most 0.155), so the association is about presence rather than dose; the veteran pilot has NO control group and measures parafunctional SIGNS rather than diagnosed bruxism, with heavy-smoking and periodontal confounding; all bruxism measures are self-report or screening instruments (RDC Axis II, Oral Behaviours Checklist), which over-report against clinical examination; and PTSD populations carry high prevalences of psychotropic medication, caffeine, tobacco and sleep disruption, all confounders. Individual claims require independently established PTSD and separately documented bruxism with clinical dental examination (wear facets, masticatory muscle findings, partner-reported grinding), a dated chronology relative to trauma exposure and PTSD onset, and exclusion of medication-induced bruxism (SSRIs, stimulants), caffeine and tobacco load, sleep-disordered breathing and pre-existing masticatory parafunction before any attribution.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized stress-arousal pathway: trauma-related hyperarousal and sleep micro-arousals are held to raise masticatory muscle activity through autonomic and corticobulbar facilitation, with awake clenching driven by sustained tension and sleep grinding by arousal events; the awake signal in the located evidence is consistent with the tension route and the sleep-bruxism null in the same adjusted model is consistent with the weaker arousal route, so whether PTSD produced any individual's bruxism remains hypothesized until the parafunction is read against the trauma, medication and sleep chronology.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Held at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at case-control and cross-sectional prevalence class with the awake-versus-sleep split carried as the controlling limitation: the catalog identity is the UMBRELLA Bruxism (Awake / Sleep) and the located adjusted evidence covers the AWAKE member only, the SLEEP member resting on prevalence excess (40.1 versus 15.3 percent) and a trauma-type gradient while the same adjusted model reports a sleep-bruxism NULL; a TARGET-SCOPE DISCLOSURE therefore applies (the slap-tear and rotator-cuff precedent): the edge's evidence is awake-centric and the sleep member is prevalence-context only. BOUNDARY AGAINST ME-34: the registry records the batch that REJECTED a bruxism-to-TMJ route on evidence grounds (PMID 9758394) and this edge does NOT reopen masticatory-joint claims; the TMD prevalences in the anchors are comorbidity context, not a claim window, and no chain to any TMJ identity is claimed. ANCHOR DISCLOSURES: the prevalence anchor is ERRATUM-LINKED (J Oral Rehabil 2024;51(5):911-914, content NOT checked here and required reading for the qualified human), carries dental-sleep-industry conflicts (SomnoMed, Sunstar, ResMed grants and a GrindCare advisory role) and an EMDR-income conflict, and measures by self-report checklist; the veteran pilot is uncontrolled and confounded by smoking and periodontal disease.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The only adjusted association (awake bruxism, OR 3.38) has a confidence interval of 1.01-11.27 in a 38-versus-38 convenience sample, and the same model reports a SLEEP BRUXISM NULL, so the umbrella target's sleep member has no adjusted support in the located evidence; all bruxism ascertainment is self-report or screening-instrument based; PTSD symptom severity correlates only poorly with bruxism severity (rs at most 0.155); the 673-patient prevalence anchor is erratum-linked with content unchecked and industry-conflicted; the 71-veteran pilot has no control group and measures parafunctional signs with smoking and periodontal confounding; and NO located anchor establishes that bruxism postdates PTSD onset in incident cohorts.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Medication-induced bruxism (SSRIs and other antidepressants, stimulants, antipsychotics) prescribed within the PTSD treatment timeline
Caffeine, tobacco and alcohol load and stimulant use, which are elevated in PTSD populations and independently raise masticatory activity
Sleep-disordered breathing and periodic limb movements as arousal sources for sleep bruxism
Pre-existing masticatory parafunction and TMD predating trauma exposure
Occlusal factors, reflux-related grinding and age-related parafunctional habits
